summary: App reported micro-billing delta after change to per-invocation metering for tool-calls
description:
Issue summary:
BrightLearn reports a subtle but consistent increase in invoiced charges starting 2026-03-01 after an internal metering rollout. Their workload is dominated by high-frequency tool-call patterns (tool-calls that wrap an embedding call + logging hook) where each user session issues hundreds of short tool invocations per minute.

Impact:
- Estimated delta ~0.6% higher than console estimates across their last monthly invoice (~$1,250 difference on a $200k invoice).
- Appears as a large number of small line items (microcharges) in the invoice reconciliation csv, causing accounting noise and reconciliation failures on their side.
- Customer concerned about scaling effect if traffic grows; requests explanation and corrective action or credit.

Environment:
- Customer in enterprise Dedicated setup (reserved pool) with production routed through us-east.
- Metering change was rolled to hosted and dedicated pools on 2026-03-01 as part of PR 2f8a3b (internal change to switch ambiguous tool-calls to per-invocation counting rather than per-inference).

Steps to reproduce / examples:
1) Query logs for org BrightLearn, hour window 2026-03-02 14:00-15:00 UTC.
2) Filter requests where payload.tool_invocations_count > 0 and each request has 3+ small tool calls (<250 tokens).
3) Compare postback usage lines with pre-rollout baseline (2026-02-25).
Observed: many requests now generate multiple meter entries where before they were batched into a single per-inference entry.

Attachments / logs:
- Attached csv excerpts provided by customer (line sampling: invoice_lines_sample.csv).
- Related commit: github.com/redwood-inference/invoice/commit/2f8a3b
- Console estimate vs finalized invoice screenshots provided by customer (sensitive attachments in ticket).
comments: 2026-03-10 10:24 - Maya Chen (support): Created ticket after customer emailed billing@redwood. Customer provided sample invoice rows and estimate screenshots. Asked for preliminary triage and whether this is an intentional metering policy change.

2026-03-10 14:01 - Liam O'Connor (billing eng): Confirmed change was part of PR 2f8a3b; intent was to make tool-calls billable individually in order to reflect compute cost per invocation. Noted rollout targeted ambiguous cases but may have been broader than planned due to route matching rule. Opening investigation to scope impact.

2026-03-11 09:12 - SRE (Priya Patel): Pulled postback samples for BrightLearn for 2026-02-24 and 2026-03-03. Early finding: the postback aggregator now emits separate meter rows for each tool invocation when the request's tool_invocations_count metadata is present, whereas previous behavior coalesced into a single "inference" row. Attaching sample counts and aggregator query IDs.

2026-03-11 16:40 - Finance (Owen Park): Customer asked for provisional credit while we investigate. Proposed temporary credit equal to observed delta (~$1,250) pending root cause confirmation. Seeking approval from billing lead.

2026-03-12 08:30 - Customer (Elena Ruiz, BrightLearn): Appreciated quick response. Requests that any fix preserve accurate cost accounting but avoid micro-line proliferation; they prefer consolidated line items for ease of downstream reconciliation. Willing to accept credit and follow-up patch schedule.
investigation_notes: Investigative query #12345 run on 2026-03-11: compared postback lines grouped by (request_id, meter_type) pre/post rollout. Showed 18% increase in number of meter rows for sessions with tool-calls.
Hypothesis A: Router rule for 'tool-call' was too permissive; any wrapper with tool_metadata flag now triggers per-invocation metering.
Hypothesis B: Aggregator dedup/aggregation key was inadvertently changed (commit 2f8a3b altered aggregation key to include 'invocation_index'), preventing coalescing of invocations into single line.
Repro script: synthetic workload posted to staging replicating BrightLearn pattern; staging showed same microcharges when the new aggregator config was applied.
Impact estimate: extrapolated across their monthly volume yields $1,100-1,400 delta depending on token distribution and tool-call frequency.
resolution: Pending: Billing lead to approve provisional credit; suggested amount $1,250 as interim relief.

Engineering action plan: revert aggregator key change in dedicated pools and implement a feature-flag to toggle per-invocation vs per-inference metering. Prefer option to emit consolidated invoice lines while keeping internal per-invocation telemetry for accuracy.

Follow-ups: 1) Post-fix reconciliations for BrightLearn full billing cycle; 2) Add regression test in metering suite to avoid broad rollouts without org-specific sampling; 3) Customer-facing note explaining policy intent and next steps.
